runtime_state_migration_contract.note: The orchestrator can stage and verify recognized authoritative SQLite state in PostgreSQL. It refuses strict cutover readiness while unresolved SQLite writers, file-backed API state, or incomplete topology gates remain. Successful staging migration does not itself authorize HA, read-only rootfs, or production cutover.

security_engine_database_contract.note: Incident response, remediation, evolution, and threat-intelligence runtime composition can use PostgreSQL with replica-aware mutation controls. Historical state now has a verified staging migration path, but production data execution, backup/restore evidence, rolling-update validation, remaining writable-path removal, and explicit cutover are still required before HA.

sqlite_connectors.note: The primary database contract can target PostgreSQL, but SQLite remains an allowed runtime backend until production cutover, data verification, rollback, backup/restore, and rolling-update gates are completed.

When Celery is enabled, distributed task results are authoritative in the Redis-backed Celery result backend; local scan-job SQLite remains a runtime writer and is an explicit runtime-state migration cutover blocker until removed or explicitly scoped.

PostgreSQL mode refreshes DB authority and serializes per-incident mutations across replicas; historical SQLite incidents can be staged with attack-chain identity materialized and verified, but production cutover remains incomplete.

PostgreSQL mode claims each plan under an advisory lock before execution so replicas cannot execute the same remediation plan concurrently; historical plan/action state now has a verified staging migration path.

PostgreSQL mode provides exactly-once completed-scan learning across replicas and historical evolution state now has a verified staging migration path. SQLite file backups are not represented as PostgreSQL backups; external backup/restore validation remains an open gate.

PostgreSQL mode serializes scheduler lease acquisition and per-indicator merge updates across replicas; historical threat-intelligence state now has a verified staging migration path, but production cutover and restore evidence remain incomplete.
The live scanner still writes scans, baselines, and findings_log to local SQLite. Those tables are explicitly recognized as cutover blockers and are not silently migrated or abandoned.

PostgreSQL mode serializes append sequence and predecessor state across replicas; migration verifies the historical chain's sequence, record hashes, predecessor links, and chain hashes before staging it in PostgreSQL. Production cutover remains incomplete.

PostgreSQL mode provides row-locked approval mutations and atomic nonce replay protection across replicas; migration validates persisted approval identity before staging records/nonces in PostgreSQL. Production cutover remains incomplete.
